On it. I'll build the cart with all twelve items, and because Leo's tree-nut rule has no exceptions, I'll check the bread, yogurt tubes, cheddar and frozen dumplings for tree nuts or 'may contain' warnings. Jess should weigh a few things. Cash flow: whether rent covers mortgage, condo fees, property tax and insurance with a buffer for vacancy and repairs. Taxes: rental income is taxable and renting can affect the principal residence exemption, so a quick accountant chat is worth it. And her plans and temperament: how long she'd hold it, whether she's happy being a landlord, and whether she'd rather lock in today's price than bet on appreciation.
Action: I can turn this into a one-page checklist or pros and cons table for you to send her.

Vamos, quiz rápido. Elige el o la: 1) ___ problema, 2) ___ mapa, 3) ___ mano, 4) ___ día, 5) ___ foto, 6) ___ tema, 7) ___ idioma, 8) ___ radio. Contesta con tus respuestas y te corrijo (y por cierto, 'Estoy en la oficina', no 'Soy').
Action: Wait for your answers, correct them with a one-line rule for each, and save the ones you miss as a repeat list.

Here's a toast: 'Neha, [partner's name], finding someone who laughs at your jokes is lucky, and finding someone who still laughs the second time is basically a miracle. You two make the rest of us look like we're not trying. Here's to great food, better stories, and only the fun kind of arguments about the dishwasher. Cheers!'
Action: Send me the partner's name and one real detail or in-joke and I'll swap it in so it sounds like you.

That sounds really draining: Tuesday morning is the one you protect, and then the Montreal day trip lands on top, with a Friday heads-up, in the same week. I'll get you sorted for Thu the 8th (I'm reading that as 8 Oct), out in the morning and home for dinner.
Action: Pull round-trip Toronto-Montreal options for Thu 8 Oct, morning out and an evening return, check Tom's invite for the bank meeting time so the arrival fits, and show you the options before booking anything.

That's the stare of a creditor. Is it dinner o'clock?

Here's a draft: 'Hey! We're heading to the playground and the market at Riverdale Park East tomorrow around 10:30. Want to come with the kids? No pressure if you've got plans.'

Will do, right after the review. On it. I don't have the Ottawa flight details in front of me, so I'll dig them out of our earlier search and email rather than guess at times or fares, and I'll read your podcast note first so the new picks match your taste.
Action: Find the Ottawa flight options we compared with driving (times and fares) in a form Sam can use for his February PD day, then send you the flights and a short list of new commute podcasts based on your note.

Done, in-store pickup it is for Biscuit's food, and Sam can grab it at Queen & Logan today. Here's the Slack draft: 'Quick reminder: release freeze runs from Thursday 12:00 to Monday 09:00. Please get anything you need merged before noon Thursday, and thanks for working around it!' Honest answer: I can't grade your Spanish fairly yet, because I don't have enough of your actual Spanish or Carlos's feedback to judge, and I'd rather not flatter you.
- Calendar rule saved: no meetings before 9:30 or after 17:00, ever.

Happy to distract. Any word from your mom yet?

Let me check rather than guess. I'll look up the observed conditions for Ottawa on Sunday the 25th and give them in Celsius and metric units only.

Sending the school council reply now. On insurance: your car is with Intact and renews each April, so I'd normally start quotes four to six weeks before renewal, but I'll check the date on the letter in case it's sooner. For cancelling, you generally need to give the insurer notice (often in writing) and have the new policy start first so you're never uninsured, but I'll confirm Intact's actual terms rather than guess.
Action: Send the school email, read the renewal letter and your Intact policy for the renewal date and cancellation terms, and set a reminder for when to start getting quotes.

Good tour questions: what are the infant staff-to-child ratios and how much staff turnover is there, and is the centre licensed. Ask about the daily routine (naps, feeding, diapering, outdoor time), the sick-child, allergy and emergency policies, and how they communicate with parents day to day. Then fees and what's included, hours and closures, how settling-in works, and where she'd be on the waitlist. And ask to watch the infant room in action.
Action: Turn this into a one-page checklist Marcus can forward to his sister.

Booking a 25-minute sync with Aisha and Diego next week in a morning slot, with your three agenda items in the invite (empty-state copy, loading skeleton, who owns the Looker link).
